title: Go: Pub/Sub Message Broker
description: Build a publish-subscribe message broker in Go using channels, topics, and wildcard matching with MQTT-style patterns.

steps.title: Topic tree data structure
steps.description: Create a `TopicNode` struct for a hierarchical topic tree. Each node has a `name string`, `children map[string]*TopicNode`, and `subscribers []chan string`. Implement `AddTopic(path)` that splits on "/" and builds the tree. Print the tree structure by walking it recursively.
hints: Use `strings.Split(path, "/")` to break a topic like "sensor/temp/room1" into segments
Build the tree by iterating segments and creating child nodes as needed

verification.successMessage: Topic tree correctly builds hierarchical paths from slash-delimited topics!
verification.failureMessage: Print the tree structure showing all topic segments with indentation.

steps.title: Subscribe with channels
steps.description: Implement a `Subscribe(topic string, ch chan string)` method on the broker. Store the channel reference in the corresponding topic node. Create a broker, subscribe to "sensor/temp/room1", and print "Subscribed to sensor/temp/room1" to confirm.
hints: Traverse the topic tree and append the channel to the node's subscribers slice
Create channels with `make(chan string, bufferSize)` to avoid blocking on publish
A buffered channel of size 10 is a reasonable default

verification.successMessage: Subscription stores the channel reference at the correct topic node!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Subscribed to <topic>' to confirm subscription was recorded.

steps.title: Publish to topic
steps.description: Implement a `Publish(topic string, message string)` method. Traverse to the topic node and send the message to all subscriber channels using a goroutine per subscriber. Subscribe two channels to different topics, publish, and print received messages from each subscriber.
hints: For each subscriber channel, launch `go func(c chan string) { c <- msg }(ch)` to avoid blocking
Use a `select` with default case to skip subscribers with full buffers

verification.successMessage: Published messages are delivered to all subscribers of the topic!

steps.title: Wildcard matching (+ and #)
steps.description: Implement MQTT-style wildcard matching. `+` matches one level, `#` matches any remaining levels. When publishing, walk the topic tree and also check wildcard subscriber nodes. Subscribe with "sensor/+/room1" and "sensor/#", publish to "sensor/temp/room1", and show both wildcard subscribers receive the message.
hints: For `+`, match any single segment at that level and check children
For `#`, collect all subscribers at the current node and all descendant nodes

verification.failureMessage: Print 'wildcard subscriber received: <message>' to show wildcard matching works.

steps.title: Durable subscriber with backlog
steps.description: Implement a `DurableSubscriber` that stores unprocessed messages in a backlog slice when the subscriber channel is full. Add `Acknowledge(id)` to remove processed messages. Print the backlog size and acknowledge some messages to show it shrinking.
hints: Each message gets a unique `uint64` ID using `sync/atomic`
Store messages in a `[]Message` slice on the subscriber struct with a mutex

verification.successMessage: Durable subscribers maintain a backlog and correctly track acknowledged messages!
verification.failureMessage: Print the backlog size after publish and after acknowledgment.
